items.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: once in New York, when you and George were up there

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, I used to work, first I used to work for Al Mastricht, 919 on Lobster Street, and I used to do all the slater work, paper hanging, plaster, that's my tray, and I knew that I'd do carbonate work. And I done all that. I went for D'Alandino real estate at 729 Newton Street. I done all that for D'Alandino real estate. And now I went for Miss Ducco at 1301 Barrett Street. She's dead, and her sister died, and all of them cats are from Miss Ducco. My father and neighbors, my parents used to be at a bigger…
Well, can you tell me, once in New York, when you and George were up there, you told me how you used to throw the big bags of coffee up, they had some sort of a little call? Yeah, yeah, sure, but...

Did it in rhythm, or how did you do that? Yes, indeed. Well, see, that time, everything you had to do was pick up. See, one man on the other side of the man there, see? Now, after so much higher, you had to throw it. You already got a little slack. You threw up there, that man put it, and then it went straight up.
